title: Anatomy of a Rust DOS application

boxes.label: shell/dos/src/main.rs
boxes.sub: wires the core to DOS and runs the scenario or the keys
boxes.text: The program SHELL.EXE is one Rust file that opens a display and an input source, builds the presenter and calls the core's Shell::handle and Shell::frame itself: the platform owns the loop.

boxes.label: Embedded scenario and fonts
boxes.sub: first-window.scn, UI.DFN, TITLE.DFN (or files with fontfile)
boxes.text: The scenario and the two .DFN faces are compiled in; the fontfile argument reads UI.DFN and TITLE.DFN from the program's directory instead and the digests must not change.

boxes.label: desk-shell
boxes.text: The shell: events in, frames out, and the scenario runner.

boxes.label: desk-wm
boxes.text: Windows, z-order, focus, dragging and the damage each change makes.

boxes.label: desk-ui, desk-font
boxes.text: Theme roles, window chrome, text drawing and the reader for .DFN faces.

boxes.label: desk-gfx
boxes.text: Rectangles, the back buffer, damage, the compositor and the frame digests.

boxes.label: desk-present
boxes.text: Presents only what changed, to a linear frame buffer (depth 8) or to the four planes of mode 12h (depth 4).

boxes.label: HAL drivers
boxes.text: Drivers written once against the HAL's traits and tested on the host against a mock port bus.

boxes.label: start, panic, cleanup
boxes.text: The entry point the stub jumps to, the panic handler (exit status 3) and the clean-up list that restores vectors and text mode before the program ends.

boxes.label: heap
boxes.text: The global allocator over memory blocks the DPMI host hands out.

boxes.label: dos
boxes.text: INT 21h wrappers. Every call that takes a pointer goes through a 32 KiB transfer buffer in conventional memory and a DPMI real-mode call.

boxes.label: dpmi
boxes.text: A hand-written client for the DPMI host: memory blocks, descriptors, locking, vectors and real-mode calls.

boxes.label: irq
boxes.text: A stub per IRQ line that calls a Rust handler and sends the end-of-interrupt; IRQ 1 is the keyboard.

boxes.label: hal
boxes.text: The DOS platform's implementations of the HAL's BIOS and display traits: real-mode calls, the VBE mode list and mode set, and the linear frame buffer mapped through DPMI 0800h.

boxes.label: dos-elf.json
boxes.text: A freestanding 32-bit ELF target (i486, SIMD off, panic = abort) with core and alloc built from source by -Zbuild-std (RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1).

boxes.label: rust-lld
boxes.text: The linker that ships with the Rust toolchain links the crates into one static ELF.

boxes.label: tools/elf2go32.py
boxes.text: Rearranges the ELF's loadable segments into the COFF image DJGPP's stub loads: no symbols or relocations are needed because the linker already resolved them.

boxes.label: DJGPP stub
boxes.text: The stub is written out by DJGPP's stubify and put in front of the image.

boxes.label: SHELL.EXE
boxes.text: The result, as the first-window result section records it (102,400 bytes). CWSDPMI.EXE is copied beside it.

boxes.label: The stub starts first
boxes.text: DOS runs SHELL.EXE; the stub at its front reads the COFF image into memory and transfers control to the entry point.

boxes.label: CWSDPMI
boxes.text: The protected-mode host that gives the program a 32-bit flat address space and the INT 31h services.

boxes.label: DOS and the BIOS
boxes.text: DOS provides files and the exit call; the video BIOS answers the VBE calls the program makes through DPMI real-mode calls.

boxes.label: Exit to DOS
boxes.text: The vectors the program hooked are restored and the screen goes back to text mode before the exit call; exit status 0 is success, 1 a failed comparison, 4 a timeout and 5 an unknown argument.

boxes.label: VGA ports and DAC
boxes.text: Direct port I/O to the VGA registers: the planes at depth 4 and the six-bit DAC palette.

boxes.label: VBE linear frame buffer
boxes.text: At depth 8 the mode is 0x101 (640 x 480 x 8), its frame buffer found at a physical address and mapped with DPMI 0800h.

boxes.label: Keyboard on IRQ 1
boxes.sub: typed by AUTOTYPE in the check
boxes.text: A protected-mode IRQ 1 handler feeds a lock-free ring; the check types 'desk' with DOSBox's AUTOTYPE and compares the screen's digest.

boxes.label: Mouse on INT 33h
boxes.text: The INT 33h driver is built and tested in spike B, but the first-window check scripts the pointer as events and never moves a mouse.

boxes.label: DOSBox Staging, headless
boxes.sub: S3 Trio64 model; the CI image's copy
boxes.text: Where every run so far happened. The capture reads back what the emulated card holds, not a picture of what DOSBox draws.

boxes.label: A real 486 PC
boxes.text: Nothing has run on a real VGA card, a real monitor or a real DOS machine.
